name: Wig CRM
tagline: A whole wig business in one offline HTML file
oneLiner: A production, Hebrew-RTL business-management system for a wig studio, delivered as a single self-contained HTML file that runs offline by double-click: clients, a two-stage appointment calendar, a per-sale cost/supplier ledger, profit tracking that never exposes cost to the customer, and rule-based reminder automations.
clientType: Small business — wig studio (custom & second-hand wigs, styling, upgrades)

framework: None — hand-rolled hash-free view router, string-template rendering
storage: File System Access API (optional local-file sync)
offline: Runs fully from file:// with no network
assets: Base64-inlined logo & favicon (no external image requests)

highlights: An entire business system delivered as one ~300 KB HTML file that opens by double-click and needs no install, no server, and no internet
Cost and supplier are attached to the sub-service (product), not to the payment, so every sale computes true profit automatically
Selling a product auto-posts a charge to that supplier's rolling ledger, keyed by the source appointment, so the supplier balance is always right with zero manual entry
Two-stage appointment flow: booked by phone with only a service, then the exact sub-service (and its price/cost) is captured on arrival
Customer profit uses charge minus cost (not paid minus cost), so a partial payment never distorts the monthly profit
Cost fields live only in a hidden internal area — the screen the customer can see never shows what a wig cost the studio
Idempotent reminder engine: one-day-before wash reminders and birthday greetings are created once each via per-rule log keys
Optional true local-file persistence via the File System Access API, with the file handle preserved across sessions in IndexedDB
Every screen rendered with plain template strings and a tiny router — no framework, no virtual DOM, no build pipeline
Full RTL Hebrew UI with a consistent rose-gold design system and forms designed to never scroll
features: Dashboard: today's appointments, open tasks, due auto-reminders, and this month's profit at a glance
Calendar: month grid of appointments and events, with Hebrew month names
Clients: contacts with statuses, groups, birthdays; CSV import and Excel export
Tasks: manual and auto-generated to-dos with priorities

Finances — four tabs: overview (income, supplier cost, expenses, net profit, open debts, trend, by-service), transactions, upcoming payments (6-month credit & supplier forecast), suppliers (rolling account)
Settings: services & price list, payment methods, cards, groups, statuses, suppliers, automations, and business branding
Client card: per-customer visit history, payments, expenses and running balance
engineeringDecisions: Model the business rule 'appointment = what was sold, payment = money in, expense = money out, supplier = what is owed' as the single source of truth
Attach cost/supplier to the sub-service so the money math survives partial payments and price changes
Regenerate the supplier ledger deterministically from appointments (delete-then-rebuild by sourceEvent key) so re-saving an appointment is always consistent
Write to localStorage on every mutation; mirror to a real file only when a handle is connected, with debounced writes
Keep all state in one JSON document to make backup, restore, and file-sync trivial
Ship zero dependencies and inline every asset so the file keeps working offline, forever, with no supply chain
